question: Can a trained network reduce feature interference by distributing the same number of non-zero weights across more neurons, and do the resulting gains persist beyond a synthetic setting?

key_findings.claim: Fixed Parameter Expansion duplicates each hidden neuron, partitions its incoming support among sparse children, duplicates outgoing weights, and prunes the small surplus so the non-zero weight count is held fixed.
key_findings.evidence: The intervention is applied after 25 warm-up epochs and both dense and expanded models receive another 25 matched epochs; masks normally remain fixed, which makes neuron count and support allocation the controlled changes.

key_findings.claim: On the eight-clause Boolean case study, clause-aware and random splitting improve test accuracy from 78.7% to 99.4% and 88.7%, respectively, while the expanded representations show more isolated clause structure.
key_findings.evidence: The first-layer Gram matrices and clause-code discussion connect the accuracy change to reduced overlap rather than simply to a larger dense parameterization.

key_findings.claim: Benefits are largest when feature demand is high relative to neuron count, and feature-capacity increases and cosine-similarity decreases track the accuracy gains.
key_findings.evidence: Width/clause sweeps over five trials show diminishing gains as dense width grows, a plateau at very high clause pressure, and regressions relating interference metrics to relative improvement.

anchors.section: Feature capacity and cosine similarity, Figure 3

key_findings.claim: The same fixed-nonzero-budget intervention improves small classifiers over frozen vision embeddings and jointly learned Boolean/CIFAR representations, but real-data feature-based splitting is only comparable to random splitting.
key_findings.evidence: FashionMNIST, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-100 and ImageNet-1k plots report improvements over dense baselines, with the strongest relative gains at narrow bottlenecks; the authors explicitly say their clustering heuristic likely does not recover true features.

method.core_idea: Treat neuron count and non-zero parameter count as separate architectural axes, then use sparse child neurons as a controlled intervention on feature collisions.
method.mechanism: Incoming edges of each trained neuron are divided among more children while outgoing connections are re-sparsified. Boolean DNF tasks provide known feature partitions; Gram structure, feature capacity, cosine similarity, and accuracy test whether reduced collisions mediate performance.
assumptions: Non-zero parameter count is the relevant capacity and memory budget even though activation and sparse-kernel costs change.
Boolean clauses are valid stand-ins for separable features and class count is a rough proxy for real feature demand.
Post-warm-up expansion and continued training provide a fair comparison to a dense model trained for the same epoch budget.

techniques.role: Partitions trained neuron supports into wider sparse child layers without adding non-zero weights.
Uses Gram matrices, feature capacity, cosine similarity, collision rates, and clause recovery as mechanistic measurements.
Varies clauses/classes and hidden width to test the predicted demand-to-neuron interaction.

evaluations.setting: Read-once monotone DNF classification with controlled clause and hidden-neuron counts.
evaluations.metric: Test accuracy, relative improvement, feature capacity, cosine similarity, collision rate and clause recovery.
evaluations.result: Clause-aligned splitting is strongest, random splitting often helps, and gains concentrate in high-superposition regimes.
evaluations.baseline: Dense classifiers with the same non-zero parameter count and matched continued training.

evaluations.setting: FashionMNIST, frozen-CLIP CIFAR/ImageNet classifiers, a jointly trained CIFAR-100 CNN, and a deeper ImageNet-1k classifier.
evaluations.metric: Accuracy at fixed non-zero weight count across widths and expansion factors.
evaluations.result: FPE generally improves narrow bottlenecks; random and heuristic feature splits are often similar on real data.
evaluations.baseline: Matched dense, DropConnect-style, non-disjoint, and larger-parameter controls reported in the main text and appendices.

limitations: Experiments are small relative to modern transformers and do not establish wall-clock or energy savings.
Feature-aligned partitions are available only in the synthetic task; the real-data heuristic does not demonstrably recover semantic features.
Expansion changes activation memory and sparse execution structure despite holding non-zero weights constant.
The intervention follows dense warm-up, so it is not evidence that the sparse expanded architecture trains equally well from scratch.
failure_modes: When the dense model already has enough neurons, expansion yields little benefit.
Splitting can fragment interacting inputs that must remain together, and later pruning can remove useful outgoing connections.
Unstructured sparse kernels may erase any systems benefit or make the expanded network slower.
reusable_insights: Parameter count alone does not identify where a model's representational bottleneck lies.
Known-feature synthetic tasks can test whether an architectural gain is mediated by reduced interference rather than merely correlated with sparsity.
Random partitions are an important control when a purported semantic grouping heuristic is used.
open_questions: Does FPE improve transformer language models at matched training FLOPs, activation memory, and wall-clock time?
Can sparse autoencoders or causal feature discovery choose partitions that consistently beat random splits?
Can support partitions be learned end to end without collapsing back into interference?

competitive_landscape.title: Toy Models of Superposition
competitive_landscape.relationship: Mechanistic foundation for feature superposition and polysemanticity.
competitive_landscape.difference: Elhage et al. characterize why sparse features share directions in toy models; the target turns that diagnosis into a fixed-nonzero-weight architectural intervention and tests task accuracy.

competitive_landscape.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct alternative for resolving polysemantic representations.
competitive_landscape.difference: Sparse autoencoders learn an external overcomplete dictionary over a fixed base model; FPE changes the base network's neuron/support structure and targets performance as well as interpretation.

competitive_landscape.title: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: Finding Sparse, Trainable Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Sparse-subnetwork predecessor under reduced parameter budgets.
competitive_landscape.difference: Lottery-ticket work identifies trainable pruned subnetworks and special initializations; FPE preserves a trained model's non-zero budget while increasing neuron count and explicitly tests feature-collision reduction.

novelty_assessment: The defensible contribution is a controlled fixed-nonzero-weight expansion experiment linking width, interference metrics, and accuracy across synthetic and modest vision settings. It is not the first account of superposition or sparse subnetworks, and practical compute efficiency at transformer scale remains unshown.
